bottleneck: Base editors were designed to avoid double-strand breaks, yet studies in mouse embryos and rice found hundreds of unintended mutations from the deaminase acting on off-target DNA and RNA. These bystander edits are harder to predict than Cas9 off-targets because they arise from the deaminase domain's intrinsic activity, not just guide RNA binding. Reliable detection methods are still maturing.
current_state: Researchers are engineering deaminases with narrower activity windows and developing better assays, but no base editor is yet proven free of widespread off-target mutations in vivo.

title: Base editors cause deaminase-driven bystander mutations
why_it_blocks: Base editing is the leading route for correcting point mutations, the most common class of pathogenic variants. Until bystander mutations are controlled, its clinical use remains a calculated risk rather than a precise medicine.
